 Programme announcement
 No items found. Iris Prize is an annual LGBTQ+ film festival in Cardiff, Wales, established in 2007. Its programme combines short and feature films with filmmaker discussions, industry events and community activity.
 The main Iris Prize funds a new LGBTQ+ short film by the winning filmmaker. The festival also works with Film4 to bring its Best British shortlist to television and streaming audiences.
 Next edition — 2027
 The festival has announced 11–17 October 2027 in Cardiff, alongside Iris Online across the UK. Submissions open on 11 January 2027. Further submission deadlines and fees are still to be announced.
 Latest completed edition — 2026
 The Cardiff festival ran from 12–18 October 2026, with the online programme running from 13–31 October. Submissions for that edition are closed. The award list below refers to 2026.

 Growing Pains at Iris Prize: Queer Youth, Change and Finding Your Voice Growing Pains brings five international queer shorts to Iris Prize 2026, followed by a Q&A with Jacob McKee, Caio Amado Soares and Daniel Neiden. Magid / Zafar Wins the £40,000 Iris Prize 2026 Luís Hindman’s Magid / Zafar wins the £40,000 Iris Prize 2026, with three international shorts also receiving special mentions. Molly Wins Best British at Iris Prize 2026 Darius Shu’s Molly wins Best British at Iris Prize 2026, alongside special mentions for Life of Kai and Yellow Bucket and three performance winners. Cultural Crossroads at Iris Prize: Queerness, Family and Belonging Cultural Crossroads brings four international queer shorts to Iris Prize 2026, followed by a Q&A with Mohammad Awad, Rizcel Gagawanan and David McDonagh. Behind Closed Doors at Iris Prize: Desire, Silence and Queer Horror Behind Closed Doors brings four queer shorts to Iris Prize 2026, with Matteo Giampetruzzi, Ashley Panton and Andin Ngwa joining the post-screening Q&A. Iris Prize Opens Its 20th Edition in Cardiff With Five New Welsh Films Iris Prize begins its 20th edition in Cardiff with five new Welsh films, Pink Portraits 2026 and reflections from Berwyn Rowlands and Tom Abell. Joe Locke to Attend Black Church Bay Welsh Premiere at Iris Prize 2026 Joe Locke joins Tom Cullen and director Rhys Marc Jones for the Welsh premiere of Black Church Bay, closing the 20th Iris Prize festival in Cardiff. Welsh Filmmakers Take Centre Stage as Iris Prize Turns 20 Welsh filmmakers take a central place at Iris Prize 2026, with new shorts on Opening Night and more Welsh talent across the Cardiff festival. One Week to Go: Iris Prize Celebrates 20 Years in Cardiff With one week to go until Iris Prize 2026 begins, founder Berwyn Rowlands looks back on 20 years of queer cinema in Cardiff. T’Nia Miller Stars in Queer Short TRY, Set for World Premiere at Iris Prize 2026 T’Nia Miller stars in queer short TRY, which will receive its world premiere during the 20th Iris Prize LGBTQ+ Film Festival’s Opening Night in Cardiff.
